A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CUB benchmark study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of context-utilisation techniques across CounterFact, NQ and DRUID, together with feature correlations, relevance-assessment results and dataset-quality analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and supplementary analyses. Their retention from v1 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The fine-tuning, prompting, multi-agent, PH3 and decoding procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retained; the longer fine-tuning, multi-agent and PH3 descriptions in v2's appendices relocate material already present in v1.

E1.justification: Evaluation still covers CounterFact, NQ and DRUID with gold, conflicting and irrelevant contexts. Fine-tuning retains SQuAD 2.0, TriviaQA, AVeriTeC and DYNAMICQA. The expanded discussion of long-context and multi-document settings introduces no evaluations in those settings.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Regular, Fine-tuning, Prompting, Multi-agent, PH3 +context, PH3 +memory, COIECD and ACD. Their participation across models and datasets is unchanged in the matched result tables.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated categorisation criteria: gold contexts no longer require agreement with model memory, and conflicting contexts now always contradict memory, replacing v1's memory-or-gold-label criterion. This changes the reported evaluation description, although Appendix B retains the original construction rules, including verdict-based DRUID conflicts. Relabelling or rerunning experiments is not established; splits, metrics and tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the CounterFact prompting analysis, irrelevant-NQ quality check, relevance-agent analysis, memorisation check and model/input-feature correlations. Moving the model-feature correlation table into the main text adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions show standard deviations for model-averaged relative performance and mark significant correlations using p < 0.05. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or new uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Matched tables retain identical numerical entries, including BCU, accuracy, relevance-assessment accuracy, memorisation rates and correlations. All five figures retain their graphical content. The rewritten results discussion preserves the findings; renumbering and relocation do not introduce new results.

T1.justification: The BCU and relative-gain definitions and the piecewise CCU equation in Appendix C are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical results or proofs that are introduced or removed in the other.

C1.justification: The abstract shifts the advertised purpose from helping practitioners identify the best CMT to diagnosing CMTs under different context conditions. v2 also explicitly claims the most extensive evaluation to date. The central benchmark contribution and findings about context-type trade-offs and inflated synthetic-dataset performance remain.

C2.justification: The expanded limitations explain why multi-document evaluation is excluded, citing difficulty disentangling document effects and incompatibility with included CMTs. Section 6.2 removes v1's practical recommendation to select ACD for retrieval systems prone to irrelevant contexts. Existing long-context, language and temporal limitations remain.

D1.justification: Detailed collection recipes, prompt templates, hyperparameter tables, fine-tuning settings, hardware and compute costs are retained. Expanded method appendices mainly consolidate existing disclosures. Dataset access identifiers and the promise of code availability upon publication remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference lists are unchanged, but v2 explicitly positions the study as the first comprehensive CMT evaluation and the most extensive comparison to date. This modestly strengthens comparative novelty positioning; v1 already stated that no dedicated CMT benchmark existed.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, benchmark framing, substantial portions of the results discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Method and dataset explanations move into appendices, including a separately titled PH3 appendix, while the limitations discussion expands substantially. These constitute broad narrative and structural revision despite stable experimental content.

P2.justification: The model-feature correlation table moves from appendix Table 6 to main-text Table 3, while the multi-agent diagram moves from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 5. Other exhibits are renumbered, several captions change, and Table 11 abbreviates context labels and adjusts layout. The figures and table contents are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: Expanded limitations and the main-text correlation table improve scope transparency and access to evidence. However, v2's assertion that conflicting contexts always contradict model memory is inconsistent with the retained verdict-based DRUID construction in Appendix B.3. With experimental evidence unchanged, the useful clarifications and reduced consistency of the benchmark description leave the net quality direction uncertain.
